To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the expression of VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP was increased in the Paget's disease tissues compared to normal skin; (b) VEGF-A expression was significantly increased in the Pagets' cells compared to normal epithelium; (c) VEGF expression was not significantly correlated with PD-ECGF expression, suggesting that the two growth factors may act independently in Paget's diseases.

the role of vascular endothelium growth factor A (VEGF-A), and platelet-derived growth factor/thymidin phosphorylase (TP/PD-ECGF), in Paget's vulvar disease, and in Paget's breast disease, is to stimulate the growth and survival of the malignant cells.
the VEGF-A/PD-ECGF/ TP pathway may play a role in the pathogenesis of Paget's disease, and that the expression of PD-ECGF/THP is associated with a poor prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiogenesis in Paget's Disease of the vulva.
the role of angiogenesis in the pathogenesis of Paget's disease.
the role of VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP in the pathogenesis of vulval Paget's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP in Paget's Disease is not fully understood.
the use of a single drug, or even a combination of two drugs, is not the best way to treat Paget's disease, but a multidrug therapy is the most effective treatment.

the role of vascular endothelium is a key component for the growth of the tumour and that the angiogenic factors VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP are involved in the angiogenesis of both Paget's disease and the underlying invasive breast cancer and vulvar squamous cell carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found VEGF-A and TP to be important in the progression of Paget's disease.
we have shown a role for VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP in the angiogenesis associated with Paget's disease, and that these angiogenic molecules are expressed in Paget's cells, and in the stroma.
we have identified two new markers for the diagnosis of Paget's disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP may be useful markers for the diagnosis and follow-up of Paget's disease.
the expression of VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP in Paget's lesions is significantly higher than in normal skin and that this is associated with an increase in angiogenesis in the lesions.
we can use a combination of VEGF-A and PD-ECGF/ TP to identify patients with Paget's disease.
